help.howitworks.switching_service_source.backTranslation: While a download is paused: Choosing another source for a file that has already started downloading is accepted and saved, but nothing starts. The service and source shown remain the current ones, and a message appears next to the service name stating where the file will go; for example Will switch on resume: Real-Debrid (rapidgator.net). Choosing again changes this message; choosing the source already in use removes the message. After you resume the download, it reads Switching: … until the switch takes effect, then the message disappears. If a download's paused files will go to different places, or the destination is unknown, no destination is shown. A file that has never started has nothing to hand over; so its new source is applied directly when the file starts. Choosing a service while paused works as described above; the only difference is that the download stays paused: a service that can take the link in use takes over immediately (the badge shows this), while a service that must first prepare a copy shows Preparing … and takes over only after you resume. These messages appear in Download activity and in Downloads rows; both kinds may appear at the same time.

help.howitworks.backup_torrents.each_deb.backTranslation: Each debrid service has a Prepare backup torrents switch. This switch is on by default for AllDebrid, Debrid-Link, Premiumize and Real-Debrid, and off by default for TorBox, which has stricter torrent limits. While the switch is on, that service also adds torrents delivered by another service, so that it is ready to take over if needed. When you move a download to another service, the torrent it started earlier is also kept as a backup instead of being removed. This uses that account's torrent slots and limits; a new download that needs a slot takes that slot back first. To reserve that service's slots for its own downloads, turn the switch off: in that case the service's backups are removed. A choice you saved earlier is kept.

Backups use that account's torrent slots and limits; a new download that needs a slot first takes that slot back.

Web links are always added as a new download. After a download has completed, been cancelled or been removed, adding the same source again starts a new download. If two downloads turn out to fetch the same content, DebridPulse can merge them; Merged appears on the merged download. If DebridPulse cannot prove that they match, Merged · Unverified appears on the merged download instead. Merging does not change who requested the download: each account's request remains its own.

help.settings.downloads.download_behavio.backTranslation: Download behavior and limits: Download folder (with Browse) and Maximum concurrent downloads. Under Advanced settings: Data checkpoint interval and Graceful stop timeout (it is recommended not to change them), Local network connections (off by default), which allows downloading from devices on your private network, and Skip local connection confirmation, which stops being asked every time. help.settings.users_access.user_accounts.backTranslation: User accounts lists each person with their role, sign-in method and whether the account is active. Add local account creates an account that signs in with a username and password. A role changed in Edit user takes effect immediately: that person's open pages reload with the new role without signing them out. Each person has a DebridPulse username separate from their display name: an OIDC account takes this name from its first sign-in, and it is the name used when signing in with a local password; in the title of the Edit user window, the pencil icon next to this name changes the name and keeps the saved password. Click an account's name to see its details and activity; a pending request can be withdrawn individually there. Disable and Remove first show how many pending download requests the account has; these requests are withdrawn, a transfer that someone else also requested continues, and finished downloads are never touched. Disabling also ends the account's sessions and stops its tokens; removing keeps the account's history and deletes the account's own notification settings. If a removed OIDC sign-in identity comes back, it gets a new account that stays disabled until you enable it. Merge combines two or more accounts into the account you choose to keep; two accounts sharing the same verified email are flagged, but only the Merge operation combines them. DebridPulse always keeps at least one usable Administrator; you cannot change your own role and cannot disable your own account.

help.settings.data_maintenance.backups.backTranslation: Backups opens the list of backups. help.settings.data_maintenance.backups_r.backTranslation: Backups and retention: scheduled backups (on by default) are taken to the Backup folder location; the Backup interval, Backup retention and Maximum backups to keep settings are under Additional backup and retention settings. A backup is removed when it becomes too old or is no longer among the newest backups you chose to keep. The same section also sets how often statistics snapshots are taken and how long they are kept: these are records, stored in DebridPulse's database, of the previous 24 hours' activity. Snapshots are not reports, are not sent anywhere and currently cannot be viewed in the interface. Run backup creates a backup immediately (only while backups are enabled).

help.settings.data_maintenance.database_.backTranslation: Database reset controls: turn on Allow database reset, press the Reset database button, type {literal} and press the Empty database button. This deletes all downloads, their requests and history, events and statistics snapshots. Accounts, passwords, OIDC links, API tokens, personal notification settings and all settings are kept. DebridPulse always creates a safety backup first and stops the operation if that backup cannot be taken. For the reset it stops running downloads and pauses processing, then brings back the previous pause state. Completed files already in your download folder are not deleted.

help.trouble.before_changing_anything.av.backTranslation: Avoid removing a download just to clear an error: DebridPulse keeps the download's source and history so it can retry or recover. help.topic.user_accounts.account_actions.backTranslation: Disabling an account ends the account's sessions and withdraws its pending download requests. Removing the account does the same and also deletes the account's own notification settings.

help.topic.integration_accounts.tokens.r.backTranslation: “Revoke” immediately prevents a token from being used to authenticate. It does not withdraw any job.

findings.note: Reviewer: "bir belirtecin kimlik doğrulamasını hemen durdurur" is ambiguous (could read as stopping verification OF the token); English: the token can no longer be used to authenticate, immediately.

help.topic.integration_accounts.what_int.backTranslation: It cannot directly pause, delete or redirect transfers, cannot change Settings and cannot see other clients' jobs.

help.topic.integration_accounts.disable_.backTranslation: Deleting the account also permanently revokes its tokens.

help.topic.delivery_profiles.jobs_files..backTranslation: Submitting a job creates a download request belonging to that application. Removing the job in the application withdraws this request or, if delivery is complete, acknowledges the delivery; the transfer itself stops only if no one else needs it.
Completed files are shared in place: no files are copied, moved or linked for the application; confirming a delivery or its expiry does not delete any file.

help.topic.deployment_type.standalone.wi.backTranslation: If no password is set, no sign-in is needed and DebridPulse is used as the built-in Administrator.

help.topic.deployment_type.what_switchin.backTranslation: No account is deleted. Other people's accounts keep their usernames, passwords, identity provider links and their saved Active or Disabled status. In the Standalone type, these accounts cannot sign in whatever that status is.
Switching clears the built-in Administrator account's password, turns off “Username and password” and OpenID Connect sign-in, and ends all browser sessions.

help.topic.event_logging.principal_contr.backTranslation: “Recorded events” is the number of events currently stored. Events are kept indefinitely; only a database reset clears them.

help.topic.backups.backups.while_enable.backTranslation: While “Enable” is on, a backup is taken every period set by “Backup interval”, and “Run backup” takes a backup immediately. The Backups list shows the stored backups; from there you can add, save, restore or remove a backup.

help.topic.backups.backups.backup.backTranslation: A backup is deleted when it is older than the “Backup retention” value or is no longer within the newest “Maximum backups to keep” count (whichever happens first).

help.topic.backups.backups.older_backups.backTranslation: Older backups are deleted according to the saved retention rules, which keep running; the settings of these rules are part of the Advanced presentation.

help.topic.backups.statistics_snapshots..backTranslation: Separately from this, DebridPulse saves a record of the previous 24 hours' activity to its own database every “Statistics snapshot interval”, and deletes snapshots older than the “Statistics snapshot retention” value. A value of 0 stops new snapshots.

help.topic.database_reset.intro.erases_d.backTranslation: Lets DebridPulse make a blank start by deleting its download history. Use it only when you really want to start over.

help.topic.heading.what_removed_kept.backTranslation: What is removed, what is kept

help.topic.database_reset.what_removed_k.backTranslation: Removed: transfers and the records of their files, download requests, external jobs, events and the Activity log, and statistics snapshots.
Kept: accounts, passwords, OpenID Connect links, API tokens, personal notification settings and all settings. Downloaded files on disk are not deleted.

help.topic.database_reset.safeguards.res.backTranslation: “Reset database” works only while “Allow database reset” is on, and asks you to confirm.

help.topic.database_reset.safeguards.pro.backTranslation: Processing is paused for the duration of the reset and then returns to its previous state. A safety backup is taken first; if the backup fails, nothing is deleted.

account.leave.message.backTranslation: Your unsaved changes in "My Account" will be lost.
